Schwartz|1977|1987|end=divorced}} | children = 1 | father = [[Richard Schaal]] }} '''Wendy Schaal''' (born July 2, 1954){{cite web |title=Schaal, Wendy 1954– |url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/education/news-wires-white-papers-and-books/schaal-wendy-1954 |website=[[Encyclopedia.com]] |publisher=[[Cengage]]}} is an American actress known for her work in [[Joe Dante]] films, such as ''[[Innerspace]]'', ''[[The 'Burbs]]'', and ''[[Small Soldiers]]''. Her other film credits include starring in ''[[Where the Boys Are '84]]'', ''[[Creature (1985 film)|Creature]]'', ''[[Going Under (1991 film)|Going Under]]'', and ''[[Munchies (film)|Munchies]]''. She had many roles on television series in the 1980s, most notably as Vicki Allen on ''[[It's a Living]]'' and Marilyn Kelsy on ''[[Airwolf]]''. Since 2005, she has primarily worked in voice acting, most notably voicing [[Francine Smith]] on the animated comedy television series ''[[American Dad!]]'' == Early years == Schaal was born in [[Chicago]], Illinois, the daughter of Lois Schaal ({{née}} Treacy) and actor [[Richard Schaal]]. Schaal's father was married to actress [[Valerie Harper]] from 1964 to 1978, during which time Harper was her stepmother.{{cite news |last=Gardella |first=Kay |title=Harper Believes Family Comedy Mainstay of TV |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1350&dat=19860411&id=DjJPAAAAIBAJ&sjid=3gIEAAAAIBAJ&pg=5186,4035107 |quote=Though she has no children of her own, Harper reared her stepdaughter, Wendy Schaal, who is now an actress |newspaper=[[Toledo Blade]] |date=April 11, 1986 |access-date=March 9, 2015}} From birth until she was five, Schaal lived with her parents in [[Crete, Illinois|Crete]], Illinois. She moved with her mother to [[Newport Beach, California]] after her parents divorced.{{cite news |title=Identifies with role |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/67189835/wendy-schaal/ |work=The Montgomery Advertiser |location=Montgomery, AL |date=December 21, 1980 |access-date=January 8, 2021 |page=127 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} Schaal studied acting with [[Viola Spolin]] in Chicago when she was nine years old, later moving to Wisconsin and then California when she was 11. When she was 14, a trip to New York to be with her father and Harper soon led her to California again when her father and stepmother chose to settle in Hollywood. Schaal earned an Associate of Arts degree from [[Los Angeles City College]], acting and working in set construction. After she attended an acting workshop led by her father, she began to work on television. ==Career== [[File:Wendy Schaal (26122820876).jpg|thumb|Wendy Schaal speaking at the 2016 [[WonderCon]] Los Angeles for [[American Dad!]], at the [[Los Angeles Convention Center]]]] Schaal's early work on television included roles on ''[[Fish (American TV series)|Fish]]'', ''[[Little House on the Prairie (1974 TV series)|Little House on the Prairie]]'', ''[[Phyllis (TV series)|Phyllis]]'', ''[[Rhoda]]'', and ''[[Welcome Back, Kotter]]''. In 1981, Schaal joined the cast of the ABC-TV series ''[[Fantasy Island]]'', portraying Julie, the niece of the program's central character, Mr. Roarke.{{cite news |last=Downey |first=Mike |title=Wendy Schaal: The New 'Tattoo' |url=https://newspaperarchive.com/other-articles-clipping-sep-30-1981-2120912/ |work=Madison Capital Times |location=Madison, WI |agency=Chicago Sun-Times News Service |date=September 30, 1981 |access-date=December 14, 2020 |page=59 |via=[[Newspaperarchive.com]]}} Her other roles on TV included Bonnie Hornback in ''[[AfterMASH]]'',{{cite book |last=Terrace |first=Vincent |title=Encyclopedia of Television Shows, 1925 through 2010 |publisher=McFarland & Company |location=Jefferson, NC |edition=2nd |date=2011 |page=19 |isbn=978-0-7864-6477-7}} Debbie Pepper in ''[[Good Grief (TV series)|Good Grief]]'',{{r|etvs|page1=404}} Vickie Allen in ''[[It's a Living]]'',{{r|etvs|page1=515}} and Liz Dooley in ''[[Nearly Departed]]''.{{r|etvs|page1=747}} She also provides the voice of Francine Smith in the cartoon series ''[[American Dad!]]''{{r|etvs|page1=36}} ==Personal life== Schaal was married to Stephen M. Schwartz on September 4, 1977, but divorced in October 1987. They have one son. ==Union activism== On March 30, 2012, the [[Screen Actors Guild]] (SAG) and the [[American Federation of Television and Radio Artists]] (AFTRA) completed a merger of equals forming a new union [[SAG-AFTRA]]. As a result of this merger, a group of actors including Schaal, fellow voice actors [[Michael Bell (actor)|Michael Bell]], [[Clancy Brown]], Schaal's former stepmother [[Valerie Harper]], and other actors including former SAG President [[Edward Asner]], [[Martin Sheen]], [[Ed Harris]], and [[Nancy Sinatra]] immediately sued the incumbent SAG President [[Ken Howard]] and several SAG Vice Presidents to overturn the merger and separate the two unions because of their claims that the election was improper.{{cite news| url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr-esq/sag-aftra-anti-merger-lawsuit-drops-demand-295573| work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]| title=SAG/AFTRA Anti Merger Lawsuit Drops Demands| first= Jonathan| last=Handel| date=February 27, 2012}} The plaintiffs dropped their lawsuit several months later.{{cite news| url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/envelope/la-xpm-2012-may-16-la-et-ct-sag-merger-20120516-story.html| website=The New York Times| last=Verrier| first=Richard| title=SAG-AFTRA merger opponents to drop lawsuit}} == Filmography == {| class="wikitable sortable" |+Film |- !
